help_topics.title: Work unit remains open: confirmation and holds
help_topics.business_question: What should I check when work is still open after picking?
help_topics.plain_answer: A pick is one step of work execution. Remaining picks, putaway, a partial quantity or a release hold can leave work unfinished. Check the header and its detail instructions before confirming anything; Work Insight confirmation has different rules for a header and a single detail.
help_topics.trigger: A user needs to understand the named configuration or warehouse action.

execution_steps.explanation: In Work Insight, find the work unit and inspect the condition, hold code, assigned user/team and individual open or in-process details. Opening a header alone does not show that all work has completed.
Confirming a header executes every open and in-process detail under it. Header or multiple-row confirmation permits full picks; partial, short, over picks and serial prompts require a single detail.

Mobile partial picks normally leave the remainder open. Close After Partial Pick can remove the remainder and close the instruction only for supported replenishment/work-order picks. It is not a general close-work switch.
Mobile Skip moves past an instruction; Pass stops processing the work unit. Neither description says that the outstanding quantity is completed. Putaway confirmation is a separate step.

Work Insight Remove Hold cannot clear wave-not-released, cycle-count-plan-not-released or work-order-not-released holds. Check the associated release process instead of treating Remove Hold as a universal remedy.

help_topics.business_question: How are users, work types and assignment order configured?
help_topics.plain_answer: A work profile groups sequence rules for the users and teams that execute work. Configure who can use it, which warehouses/zones it covers, then the numbered rules that choose work and control picking and putaway. A user can be associated with one work profile at a time.

Sequences run in numeric order. Choose work types for each sequence; selecting none means all work types. The next sequence is used when available work for the current types is completed.

Choose User Initiated, Cart Picking or System Initiated. From Assign Method orders system-directed work by the documented priority/location/FIFO combinations. To Assign Method selects LIFO or location order for putaway.

Set the container picking method and putaway options for the intended operation. Automatic Putaway and Consolidation After Putaway are not simultaneously selectable; automatic putaway is unsupported for dock-management work.

help_topics.plain_answer: First distinguish a field-validation failure from a short pick. help_topics.title: Using the Packing screen
help_topics.business_question: How do I pack items and understand an empty packing grid?
help_topics.plain_answer: Initiate the shipment or other configured identifier, choose the container, identify the item and quantity, then Pack. The screen shows open lines for that entity. No lines left to pack, a different initiation field, an unreleased wave or line eligibility can explain why the expected work is absent.

execution_steps.explanation: Check Packing Preferences Initiation Field: it may expect shipment number, ERP order or invoice. After initiation the screen lists open lines; if nothing remains to pack it reports no available lines.

Choose Existing for an associated packed container or New for a new one. Manual container assignment allows an entered ID; System creates the ID. An existing container keeps its established container type.
With Validate Item enabled, scan/enter the item or cross-reference and quantity. Otherwise select the grid row and use quantity controls. Read header instructions and any line instruction popup.
Pack applies the selected quantity. Pack All applies all remaining item quantities. Completed lines leave the grid; totals update. Serial-tracked and catch-weight items can require additional entry.
Use the Error-column checkbox to read a packing error. The Close button opens Close Container after the container is completely packed; it does not itself establish successful closure.

help_topics.plain_answer: Read the close error first. Documented causes include pending or failed QC, pending VAS under the applicable preference, and scale or weight handling. help_topics.title: Desktop packing and mobile picking/closing settings
help_topics.business_question: Do packing preferences make desktop and mobile workflows identical?
help_topics.plain_answer: No. Desktop Packing enters shipment lines into containers, while mobile can pick directly into shipping containers through work-profile settings and close them through a separate screen. Some preferences apply across flows; other controls are explicitly restricted to a screen.
help_topics.trigger: A user needs to understand the named configuration or warehouse action.
input_context: The screen/action name, relevant preference or work profile, and exact message without credentials or transactional exports.

execution_steps.explanation: For desktop Packing, check the assigned packing preference: initiation, status range, item/quantity entry and container assignment.

For mobile pick/pack, check Work Profile Container Picking Method and Work Special Handling verification/override. Pick Into Shipping Container, Pick Into Tote and no RF pick/pack describe different behaviors.
Mobile Close Container takes a container ID and displays system/actual weight. The operator can use calculated weight or enter actual weight; tolerance can require confirmation.

The retained Packing Preferences article limits its described QC tab settings to the full-screen QC Workbench and excludes RF Shipping Container QC. It limits create-container-during-close to the specified remote-desktop menu path. Do not transfer these options to every mobile screen.

configuration_dependencies: Packing preference, work profile, Work Special Handling, security and the exact screen being used.
expected_results: A source-bound explanation of the applicable options and the next check.
explanation_paths: Name the screen and intended action first: Packing, mobile work execution, Close Container or QC. Check the settings documented for that flow.

help_topics.title: Understanding lot, license-plate and serial prompts
help_topics.business_question: Why does one picking or packing flow request tracking details?
help_topics.plain_answer: Tracking prompts depend on both the item and the operation’s configuration. Mobile lot and license-plate verification comes from Work Special Handling; desktop packing can prompt for serials based on outbound or inventory tracking. Grouped work and full-unit containers have documented exceptions.
help_topics.trigger: A user needs to understand the named configuration or warehouse action.
input_context: The screen/action name, relevant preference or work profile, and exact message without credentials or transactional exports.

execution_steps.explanation: Mobile verifies the lot for lot-controlled quantities and the LP for LP-tracked locations when the relevant verification is configured. Each enabled field is validated before the instruction is submitted.

For receipt putaway, parent locating can group nested containers going to the same destination without honoring item/lot verification; child locating honors those verifications. Entire Quantity also has a quantity-verification exception.

Packing prompts for serials when configured for outbound or inventory tracking. Mobile full-unit containers created in the wave have a documented no-serial-prompt exception; do not treat every missing prompt as a fault.

In full-screen QC, Lot Verification Required changes the entry fields and item/lot grouping. The documentation advises against switching it off during an active inspection because failed quantities can lose their correct lot association.

configuration_dependencies: Item/location tracking, Work Special Handling, grouping/locating method and the specific packing or QC flow.
expected_results: A source-bound explanation of the applicable options and the next check.
explanation_paths: Compare the exact tracking mode, work type and grouped/full-unit state before changing a verification flag.

help_topics.title: Describing a runtime problem for support
help_topics.business_question: What details help explain a warehouse action that failed?
help_topics.plain_answer: Describe the exact screen, action, message and point where progress stopped. Work confirmation, packing, QC/VAS checks, close-container weight and print triggers are separate stages. A small, sanitized description lets support select the relevant configuration instead of guessing from a generic symptom.
help_topics.trigger: A user needs to understand the named configuration or warehouse action.
input_context: The screen/action name, relevant preference or work profile, and exact message without credentials or transactional exports.

execution_steps.explanation: For work execution, note header versus detail, work type, remaining pick/putaway step, hold indication and the field being verified. Say whether a success message appeared or the screen advanced after submission.
For packing, record the initiation field used, whether lines remain, Status Info and the specific Error-column message. For close, identify QC/VAS and manual/scale weight conditions.
For configuration, give the setting label, screen/tab, intended result and the applicable preference/profile scope. A total count of profiles does not identify which one applied.

For printing, distinguish work start, close and last-container print triggers. Record document type, assigned printer and the observed error without assuming that a successful close means printing succeeded.

configuration_dependencies: The relevant preference/profile and permission depend on the action.
expected_results: A source-bound explanation of the applicable options and the next check.
explanation_paths: Suggested support summary: screen/action; expected result; exact message; last successful step; applicable preference/profile; whether it affects one flow or several. Omit credentials, personal data and transaction exports.
